algorithm_witness.initialization: Initialize two empty persistent TreeEstimate instances and zero separate counters; abort before any evaluation exceeding its cap.
algorithm_witness.stopping: At most T iterations; return bottom on iteration timeout or resource abort. Each sample drawn by TreeEstimate is evaluated at most twice.
algorithm_witness.update: At x_t estimate H_t to gamma/4. If lambda_min(H_t)<-3gamma/4, choose a unit minimum eigenvector v_t and set x_(t+1)=x_t+s_t(gamma/L2)v_t with a new independent uniform sign. Otherwise estimate g_t to epsilon/4; if ||g_t||<=3epsilon/4 return x_t; else set x_(t+1)=x_t-(epsilon/(4L1))g_t/||g_t||.

application_guidance.input_pattern: Independent-tolerance stochastic SOSP with uniform sample regularity and retained scalar sample losses.
read_original_when: Changing oracle permissions, sample regularity, norm, stopping times, scale dependence or budget convention.
sensitive_conditions: Complete Hessian is not one HVP.
Both edge endpoints precede the sample draw.
Pathwise caps and per-instance success have different roles.
Do not erase mixed terms from the separate budgets.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Per-instance success >=2/3; separate deterministic raw evaluation caps on all paths.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Explicit budgets retain scales; simplified tilde bounds fix positive scales and suppress logarithms including dimension, not polynomial dimension factors.
complexity_scope.oracle: Persistent opaque sample handles, gradient and complete Hessian charged separately; arbitrary reuse permitted though this upper witness needs at most two evaluations per drawn sample.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Point with both gradient and minimum-eigenvalue conditions; bottom is failure.
complexity_scope.resource: N_g gradient evaluations and N_H complete-Hessian evaluations, and their sum. Endpoints charged separately; matrix computation free.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Upper witness is Algorithm 1 with Algorithm 2; not every adaptive algorithm.

content.intended_use: Supply the selected literature's explicit all-path upper budgets and its implementable optimization witness.

proofs.locator: Lemmas 1–2; Section 5.2 pp.12–14; Appendix B pp.27–28
map: Import Lemma 1's simultaneous conditional-concentration interface and Lemma 2's stopped-time charging bound with their hypotheses and batch sizes as recorded in the linked proof_method.

Accurate gradient steps decrease f by at least d_g=3epsilon^2/(32L1); the two curvature signs cancel the linear Taylor term and give conditional decrease at least d_H=gamma^3/(12L2^2). Stop an analytical shadow before its first inaccurate step, and upon return or the iteration cap.

Telescoping gives d_g E K_g+d_H E K_H<=Delta. Predictable drift has E D<=8Delta/(3epsilon), and signed curvature energy E V<=12Delta/gamma. The shadow has <=K_g+1 gradient checkpoints and <=K_g+K_H+1 Hessian checkpoints.

Apply Lemma 2 separately with (sigma_g,L1,epsilon/4) and (sigma_H,L2,gamma/4). Root costs, drift, martingale energy and checkpoint ceilings give exactly the terms in B_g and B_H up to the stated logarithmic multiplier.

Appendix B couples the implementable capped run to the shadow: combined estimator failure <=1/48, iteration timeout <=1/48, and each resource overflow <=1/48 by Markov on shadow costs. Thus success >=1-4/48>2/3. The counters enforce caps even on bad trajectories.
At return, triangle and eigenvalue perturbation bounds certify both conditions. Weighted AM–GM absorbs cross-terms only in the total rate, not the separate budgets.
proofs.omitted_details: Matrix Hoeffding is an imported literature tool; no independent reproof of that tool or whole-paper certification.
proofs.reading_coverage: Personally inspected pp.6–12 native images and read original-PDF upper-bound text pp.13–14, Appendix A.1 and Appendix B.

assumptions: Assumption 1: f is bounded below and f(x0)-inf f<=Delta.
Assumption 2: on a common probability-one set, F(.;xi) is C^2 and for all x,y, ||grad F(x;xi)-grad F(y;xi)||<=L1||x-y|| and ||Hess F(x;xi)-Hess F(y;xi)||<=L2||x-y||.
Assumption 3: f is C^2 and differentiation commutes with expectation through order two, at every x.
Assumption 4: on a common probability-one set, for all x, ||grad F(x;xi)-grad f(x)||<=sigma_g and ||Hess F(x;xi)-Hess f(x)||<=sigma_H.
Assumption 5: sup_x||grad f(x)||<=G. The six public scale bounds are positive.
Every TreeEstimate edge uses an independent fresh batch drawn only after both endpoints have been determined, and uses the same sample at its two endpoints.
statement.conclusion: Define B_g=1+Delta L1/epsilon^2+sigma_g^2/epsilon^2+sigma_g L1 Delta/epsilon^3+L1^2 Delta/(epsilon^2 gamma), and B_H=1+Delta L1/epsilon^2+sigma_H^2/gamma^2+sigma_H L2 Delta/(epsilon gamma^2)+2 L2^2 Delta/gamma^3. Set T=1+ceil(48 Delta(32 L1/(3 epsilon^2)+12 L2^2/gamma^3)), scriptL=1+log(C(d+1)(T+1)), Q_g=ceil(48 C scriptL^4 B_g), Q_H=ceil(48 C scriptL^4 B_H). With Lemma 1 batches, error targets epsilon/4 and gamma/4 and failure probability 1/96 per tree, Algorithm 1 has N_g<=Q_g and N_H<=Q_H on every path and returns an (epsilon,gamma)-SOSP with probability >=2/3 on every instance. For fixed positive scales, N_g=tilde-O(epsilon^-3+epsilon^-2 gamma^-1), N_H=tilde-O(epsilon^-2+epsilon^-1 gamma^-2+gamma^-3), hence N_g+N_H=tilde-O(epsilon^-3+gamma^-3).
statement.objects_and_definitions: On R^d use Euclidean vector and induced operator norms. A measurable scalar loss F(x;xi) has finite expectation f(x)=E F(x;xi) at every x and a specified initial point x0. An (epsilon,gamma)-SOSP satisfies ||grad f(x)||<=epsilon and lambda_min(Hess f(x))>=-gamma. Failure symbol bottom counts as failure. An opaque handle retains one independent sample, is free to request and reveals no numerical information. Each gradient or complete-Hessian evaluation costs one; simultaneous derivatives cost two; each same-sample two-point difference costs two. Handles permit arbitrary adaptive reuse. No function values or third derivatives are supplied; computation is free.
statement.parameter_domains: Public positive Delta,L1,L2,sigma_g,sigma_H,G; arbitrary finite integer d>=1; independent epsilon,gamma in (0,1]. C is sufficiently large and numerical.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every admissible instance, d>=1 and 0<epsilon,gamma<=1, there is a universal numerical C>=1 for the stated tuning. Algorithm 1 uses independent tree batches and independent uniform curvature signs. Its success probability includes oracle and private randomness. The separate caps hold on every execution, including failures.
